Go closes per-call options to SDK-owned headers, preserves original source ownership and exposes context/error explicitly. It does not reproduce injected Python sessions, custom Resource URI/adapter selection or automatic Resource microversion negotiation.

No new metadata-specific microversion gate is introduced. Fixed Cinder 27.0.0 proves v3 routes and Volume GET/conditional collection PUT ETag at 3.15+, not current legacy v2 deployment support or an equivalent Snapshot ETag policy; caller/server own that condition.

Literal ID/key components are escaped once and invalid route inputs are rejected. Mock routing evidence is not a guarantee of encoded slash/dot handling through a real proxy/WSGI or of server key/length policy acceptance.

Python set_metadata caches the request delta and returns self rather than translating the complete merged response. Go Merge and explicit Replace return server values, have no cached lifecycle, and send metadata:{} for nil/empty inputs; native Snapshot omitempty behavior remains separate.
remaining: Existing arbitrary Volume/Snapshot Resource inputs, custom subclasses/base_path/_uri and injected session/adapter selection are not accepted and mutated by this scope; their seeded response/cache identity branch remains unmapped.

Inherited mutable MetadataMixin/Resource descriptor coercion, cached metadata update/pop behavior and wider dirty/cache lifecycle are not implemented. The tested owned string-map HTTP behavior must not be treated as full Resource parity.

contracts.behavior: WaitForServer supplies ACTIVE, exact case-insensitive ERROR, two-second polling and120-second SDK timeout. WaitForServerState keeps the same server-specific timeout with an explicit target; it is distinct from unlimited generic Compute WaitForState. The returned model is the actual native observation, not a cached supplied Python Resource.

Target state comparison precedes failure comparison. WithFailureStates replaces the exact case-insensitive default list, and an empty list disables state failure checks. error_deleting/error_extending, failed or killed are not inferred as additional service failures. Captured failure-state values remain independent of later caller slice mutations.

SDK defaults are prepended and concrete caller resource.WaitOption values apply last. WithUnlimitedWait removes a finite default, a later positive WithTimeout reinstates a bound, and parent context deadlines and cancellation remain effective. No application status adapter or polling builder is required.

The default polling interval is two seconds and a positive caller interval replaces it. Nil context or collection, invalid refs/targets/options, unsupported selected attributes and canceled context fail without HTTP. Callback cancellation and active-fetch cancellation stop before any further poll.

Status selection uses an exported string field and can also select deletion completion. Server canonical integer progress reports native values; absent canonical progress reports zero. Cinder-v3 Snapshot uses the noncanonical os-extended-snapshot-attributes:progress string tag, so callback reports zero without parsing that string. Successful terminal, failure and HTTP-error observations do not invoke the callback.

Explicit ID is stable even when response ID differs. Existing Name lookup resolves once, retains the native list/name-query boundary, and state waiting reports its initial List observation before fixed-ID GETs. Selected ResourceBase/reverse prefix, configured ordinary headers/microversion, caller context/middleware and the original live Provider token remain in use; no response-driven route or model synthesis occurs.

Fresh lookup failures remain errors rather than a successful target model. The shared read gate preserves original terminal URL/accepted-response/JSON/read/context causes even when nested native404 or adapter-owned ErrNotFound is discoverable. Actual direct403 or transport-wrapped404 terminates the service deletion observation after one request. Successful missing state fetches return a nonpanic error; successful nil deletion fetches complete.

Existing common Collection.Wait/WaitDeleted and generated WaitFor/WaitForDeletion retain their five-minute deadline and original binding failure predicate. Native WaitForStatus retains its error-only callable and native predicate-first behavior, including original caller context; source one-second/exact-case behavior is not replaced by this service policy. This is preservation evidence, not a separate native-operation status promotion.

A real HTTP payload request uses the effective ResourceBase without metadata or name lookup, returns exact binary or empty []byte, reads the accepted response and closes it exactly once before return. Callers own bytes without a response Close obligation.

No options and empty full options retain native Accept text/plain; nonempty and final replacement options select Accept. Ordinary vendor headers and live authentication survive, response Content-Type does not decode bytes, and original ServiceClient MoreHeaders may override Accept.

Nil and failing options, unsupported body/query/argument extensions, invalid headers and case-insensitive Accept extension conflicts return nil bytes with preserved errors.Is and GetPayload/secrets OperationError before any HTTP request.

Only native HTTP200 succeeds. Physical201/204/404 errors retain native actual status, response headers and raw body through the wrapper, with one request and one native body close; no metadata fallback is introduced.

An accepted response Read failure including context.Canceled discards partial bytes, preserves the wrapped cause and closes once without invoking native RetryFunc. An accepted response Close error is ignored and exact successful bytes are returned, following pinned native Extract.

Native 401 reauthentication, 429 backoff, 503 RetryFunc and transport retry remain provider-owned. Prepared typed Accept and extensions survive native replay with refreshed authentication, while explicit native request-option header replacement and OmitHeaders retain their existing behavior.

Original HTTPClient redirect policy is retained: 307 may be rejected as a native status error or followed with the caller-modified Accept to return the second payload, without adding a metadata workflow.

Actual compiled pinned native types and source produce []byte/error extraction for Barbican GetPayload with exactly one Extract and no OpenDownload; Swift typed-header and Glance live-body downloads keep their existing download policy and generated declarations. Existing GetPayload option helpers remain present.

All four actual native request, options-builder, URL and consuming Extract declaration hashes are checked. Missing source or changes to Accept default, HTTP200 policy, KeepResponseBody, header serialization, route, ReadAll or Close fail generation validation.

The typed native request/options/result/Extract graph must remain exact; changes to content-type type/tag/fields, builder return/receiver, result embedding/body/fields, extractor receiver/bytes or request context/client/id/variadic parameters fail the source/type/emission gates. Original HTTPClient redirect policy either returns the native307 status error or follows with the caller-edited header to return a boolean; no SDK fallback route is added.

Typed Wait consumes selected Neutron or bounded legacy Nova dispatch after owned raw actual ACTIVE readiness. Neutron requires actual IP ACTIVE; Nova has no IP status and retains actual model/action evidence. Both synchronous lanes require per-item exact raw ACTIVE-server target convergence; clean automatic skips have no assignment/Observed=false. Item-time Observed does not prove simultaneous final presence. Full source Resource/default/fallback behavior remains partial.

Earlier guarded named-creation evidence retains native typed models and200/204/300 list codes but owns page continuation and accepted Read/Close/source errors. Standalone Wait takes the supplied ID rather than completing ordinary cloud get_server name/filter/defaultquery/interface expansion; flavor-name creation keeps its existing defaults.
remaining: Complete dynamic Server/Resource inputs, full cloud get_server lookup/defaultquery/interface expansion and broad lookup-Exception/None retry beyond the new typed supplied-ID raw waiter. Compare the complete fault/extra_data taxonomy and all state/address/nullable inputs. Standalone180-second/five-second defaults now exist, but Go raw terminal-error, noDELETE and zero-row policies remain deliberate differences.

Compare full selected IP/default/fixed/NAT/reuse forwarding and shared configured network/service/flags/cache/source policy plus Nova-network fallback beyond bounded typed Neutron/Nova integration. Standalone Wait and automatic creation consume the shared dispatch, with new Neutron/Nova upper success fixtures limited to explicit lists; ordinary Servers.Create and the full cloud dispatch/model surface remain separate.

Compare refreshed Nova public/private/interface selection and Resource/Munch/session/model normalization, integer remaining-budget behavior and timeout/unlimited/parent/lookup/error/cleanup ordering beyond the current standalone and creation fixtures. Bounded exact raw observation and known partial results do not close these full cloud Wait contracts.

contracts.behavior: Shared discovery classifies IPv4 with router:external or provider:physical_network and IPv6 with router:external only, unless configured name-or-ID family overrides apply. Floating IPv4 candidates are router-external networks or the first configured NAT source; configured source/destination/default roles remain distinct from ordinary family roles.

An explicit NAT destination skips subnet discovery. Without one, all subnet pages are consumed and the last network in network response order with a nonempty gateway subnet becomes the NAT destination, independent of subnet ip_version. Configured NAT/default name-or-ID selection rejects missing, duplicate or cross-kind ambiguous matches; the first configured NAT source is used.

Unfiltered network discovery and conditional subnet discovery consume linked empty and later pages. Unsafe network IDs, invalid router extension decoding, later network403, subnet403 and repeated continuation links return errors without a partial snapshot; failed attempts remain retryable. Native204 returns an empty successful discovery.

All ten Connection role getters share one successful discovery and return independent owned native-plus-extension models. Aggregate getters concatenate IPv4 then IPv6 with duplicate entries retained. Caller changes do not modify cached roles, and tags/subnets/availability-zone-hints retain explicit empty versus null native array presence.

Concurrent uncached discoveries share one in-flight request and return independent models. A waiting follower can reach its own context deadline without canceling the leader. Reset advances the cache generation so a successful already-running discovery cannot repopulate the cache, while the existing caller still receives its result; subsequent concurrent cached calls issue no new request.

Typed use-external/use-internal flags default enabled and preserve ordered replacement. Both disabled returns empty roles before client/catalog/HTTP access; disabling only external still discovers both families when internal is enabled. Connection nil/canceled context fails before lookup, clean pointer or value ErrEndpointNotFound yields empty roles, and other catalog errors remain inspectable.

Role selectors are frozen with the same cloud/secure/public snapshot as native authentication. YAML family flags inherit routes_externally unless overridden; a typed WithNetworkRoles policy replaces the YAML role configuration and its default selector, and an empty typed replacement clears configured roles/default. Configured default NIC selection now consumes the same successful role snapshot; explicit typed default names retain their separate exact-name lookup.

Owned configured-network slices can be reused after caller mutation. Nil options, empty names and multiple default/NAT-destination declarations fail before discovery; a later replacement does not hide an earlier invalid option. Explicit Reset invalidates a completed Connection role cache without making a mutation request.

YAML boolean false and case-insensitive string false disable discovery before network HTTP. An explicit typed policy replaces those flags and restores discovery; a numeric YAML flag is rejected as ErrInvalidOption. Direct role discovery rejects nil or providerless clients before native HTTP.

High-level FloatingIPs.Create and Ensure consume shared configured or inferred NAT destination only without explicit port/fixed/NAT selection and with multiple ports owned by the requested server. All port pages are consumed first and foreign ports are excluded. Successful NAT discovery is reused but ports are listed on each call; Reset changes the chosen destination while preserving the actual allocation body.

Owned port count precedes IPv4 filtering, so an IPv6-only second port requires a NAT role. No NAT role returns ErrAmbiguous with sorted owned port IDs; a selected network absent from ports returns ErrNotFound; multiple selected IPv4 pairs remain ErrAmbiguous. Role403, later port403 and subnet cancellation prevent allocation without fallback or cleanup.

A single owned port or explicit fixed address, port or NAT destination bypasses automatic NAT role discovery despite an invalid configured policy elsewhere. Explicit port performs its GET rather than port listing; explicit NAT retains network_id filtering. An external Name retains the router:external/exact-name lane, while an explicit external ID needs no network-role inventory.

Connection CreateWithFloatingIP uses a single successful configured role inventory for its default NIC, floating source and NAT destination, including a configured source without router:external. Role lookup finishes before Nova POST; actual server ACTIVE precedes port and floating-IP requests, and actual floating-IP ACTIVE remains mandatory. A role403 returns no created resource; a later port403 preserves the known ACTIVE Server with nil assignment and the original HTTP cause, without allocation or cleanup.

Owned high Service CreateNetwork/UpdateNetwork/DeleteNetwork and the existing Networks.Delete adapter invalidate shared roles after accepted mutations. The actual matrix primes a configured default role, observes a new inventory after success or high-delete clean404 after a found lookup, and retains the original inventory after403/409/412, failed no-option lookup, or direct Collection404. A successful no-option Update performs its lookup and reset without PUT; initial missing ID/Name high Delete returns false without mutation or reset.

Accepted mutation read/Close/context/source or decode/ID errors preserve the actual response evidence and invalidate the originally owned role cache without another mutation caused by that error. Create/Update malformed/null/missing or wrong-shaped network bodies return an inspectable ResponseError; decoded unsafe or mismatched Update IDs retain the partial model. Delete keeps true plus an accepted response error. Public role/collection replacements during accepted Close are errors but cannot redirect the cache reset to a replacement.

A representative accepted Create resets while an earlier role inventory is in flight: that earlier caller still receives its original result, but the old generation cannot repopulate cache. The next configured default lookup reads a new inventory and repeated lookup uses that new cache. This is the actual Create/Reset fixture, not separate mutation-race coverage for every CRUD method or every getter.

The Connection-cached high Network Service resets the same role cache after Create, Update and Delete. A later getter reads a new configured inventory, and Nova default NIC plus floating source/NAT allocation consume that same refreshed inventory without manual Reset. The fixture checks actual Nova and Neutron request fields and exactly two inventory reads.

differences: The SDK exposes context-aware Connection getters returning owned native-plus-router/provider models and typed nullable pointers; Python returns mutable Network Resources and cached list/object identities. Ordinary generated Networks model behavior is unchanged. This bounded role model does not emulate all nullable descriptors, unknown properties, location or session state.

Go configured-role validation accepts a matching name OR ID consistently. Pinned classification accepts either, but its subsequent external/internal family validation checks only selected names and can reject ID-only selectors. Go also rejects unsafe IDs and preserves missing/ambiguous and decoding errors rather than incidental dynamic-input behavior.

Go caches only successful discovery, coalesces in-flight work, lets followers use their own contexts, and uses Reset generations to prevent a pre-reset flight from restoring the cache. Python serializes shared discovery with a lock and can swallow SDKException into sticky empty results. Owned returns and observable/retryable errors are deliberate Go policies.

Aggregate results retain the source IPv4-then-IPv6 order and duplicates; family classification reflects routing configuration and network extensions, not discovered subnet address families. The NAT destination inference preserves the source last-network-with-gateway rule.

Go flags are strict typed booleans; the YAML parser accepts boolean/string values via its explicit conversion policy. Pinned cloud use_* accessors store and return raw configured values, whose Python truthiness can differ. Both-disabled skips discovery; a single disabled flag does not remove that family after discovery.

These consumers do not implement private/floating-source flags or automatic IP need/skip decisions.

Consuming shared roles does not complete create_server/add_ips_to_server/get_active_server/wait_for_server.

contracts.behavior: Shared discovery classifies IPv4 with router:external or provider:physical_network and IPv6 with router:external only, unless configured name-or-ID family overrides apply. Floating IPv4 candidates are router-external networks or the first configured NAT source; configured source/destination/default roles remain distinct from ordinary family roles.

An explicit NAT destination skips subnet discovery. Without one, all subnet pages are consumed and the last network in network response order with a nonempty gateway subnet becomes the NAT destination, independent of subnet ip_version. Configured NAT/default name-or-ID selection rejects missing, duplicate or cross-kind ambiguous matches; the first configured NAT source is used.

Unfiltered network discovery and conditional subnet discovery consume linked empty and later pages. Unsafe network IDs, invalid router extension decoding, later network403, subnet403 and repeated continuation links return errors without a partial snapshot; failed attempts remain retryable. Native204 returns an empty successful discovery.

All ten Connection role getters share one successful discovery and return independent owned native-plus-extension models. Aggregate getters concatenate IPv4 then IPv6 with duplicate entries retained. Caller changes do not modify cached roles, and tags/subnets/availability-zone-hints retain explicit empty versus null native array presence.

Concurrent uncached discoveries share one in-flight request and return independent models. A waiting follower can reach its own context deadline without canceling the leader. Reset advances the cache generation so a successful already-running discovery cannot repopulate the cache, while the existing caller still receives its result; subsequent concurrent cached calls issue no new request.

Typed use-external/use-internal flags default enabled and preserve ordered replacement. Both disabled returns empty roles before client/catalog/HTTP access; disabling only external still discovers both families when internal is enabled. Connection nil/canceled context fails before lookup, clean pointer or value ErrEndpointNotFound yields empty roles, and other catalog errors remain inspectable.

Role selectors are frozen with the same cloud/secure/public snapshot as native authentication. YAML family flags inherit routes_externally unless overridden; a typed WithNetworkRoles policy replaces the YAML role configuration and its default selector, and an empty typed replacement clears configured roles/default. Configured default NIC selection now consumes the same successful role snapshot; explicit typed default names retain their separate exact-name lookup.

Owned configured-network slices can be reused after caller mutation. Nil options, empty names and multiple default/NAT-destination declarations fail before discovery; a later replacement does not hide an earlier invalid option. Explicit Reset invalidates a completed Connection role cache without making a mutation request.

YAML boolean false and case-insensitive string false disable discovery before network HTTP. An explicit typed policy replaces those flags and restores discovery; a numeric YAML flag is rejected as ErrInvalidOption. Direct role discovery rejects nil or providerless clients before native HTTP.

Owned high Service CreateNetwork/UpdateNetwork/DeleteNetwork and the existing Networks.Delete adapter invalidate shared roles after accepted mutations. The actual matrix primes a configured default role, observes a new inventory after success or high-delete clean404 after a found lookup, and retains the original inventory after403/409/412, failed no-option lookup, or direct Collection404. A successful no-option Update performs its lookup and reset without PUT; initial missing ID/Name high Delete returns false without mutation or reset.

Accepted mutation read/Close/context/source or decode/ID errors preserve the actual response evidence and invalidate the originally owned role cache without another mutation caused by that error. Create/Update malformed/null/missing or wrong-shaped network bodies return an inspectable ResponseError; decoded unsafe or mismatched Update IDs retain the partial model. Delete keeps true plus an accepted response error. Public role/collection replacements during accepted Close are errors but cannot redirect the cache reset to a replacement.

A representative accepted Create resets while an earlier role inventory is in flight: that earlier caller still receives its original result, but the old generation cannot repopulate cache. The next configured default lookup reads a new inventory and repeated lookup uses that new cache. This is the actual Create/Reset fixture, not separate mutation-race coverage for every CRUD method or every getter.

The Connection-cached high Network Service resets the same role cache after Create, Update and Delete. A later getter reads a new configured inventory, and Nova default NIC plus floating source/NAT allocation consume that same refreshed inventory without manual Reset. The fixture checks actual Nova and Neutron request fields and exactly two inventory reads.

differences: The SDK exposes context-aware Connection getters returning owned native-plus-router/provider models and typed nullable pointers; Python returns mutable Network Resources and cached list/object identities. Ordinary generated Networks model behavior is unchanged. This bounded role model does not emulate all nullable descriptors, unknown properties, location or session state.

Go configured-role validation accepts a matching name OR ID consistently. Pinned classification accepts either, but its subsequent external/internal family validation checks only selected names and can reject ID-only selectors. Go also rejects unsafe IDs and preserves missing/ambiguous and decoding errors rather than incidental dynamic-input behavior.

Go caches only successful discovery, coalesces in-flight work, lets followers use their own contexts, and uses Reset generations to prevent a pre-reset flight from restoring the cache. Python serializes shared discovery with a lock and can swallow SDKException into sticky empty results. Owned returns and observable/retryable errors are deliberate Go policies.

Aggregate results retain the source IPv4-then-IPv6 order and duplicates; family classification reflects routing configuration and network extensions, not discovered subnet address families. The NAT destination inference preserves the source last-network-with-gateway rule.

Go flags are strict typed booleans; the YAML parser accepts boolean/string values via its explicit conversion policy. Pinned cloud use_* accessors store and return raw configured values, whose Python truthiness can differ. Both-disabled skips discovery; a single disabled flag does not remove that family after discovery.

These consumers do not implement private/floating-source flags or automatic IP need/skip decisions.

The exact DELETE/GET/DELETE/GET order uses Network only, and both accepted attempts retain actual204 proof, verified flags and one query page each.

Retries=0 and a zero-valued bulk options replacement issue one accepted DELETE202 and skip verification, with no LastVerification, Absent or Down assertion. Negative retry -5 issues one DELETE plus public verification and completes on absence. Malformed passive DELETE body is preserved as response evidence without requiring a JSON floating-IP model. Pure preparation defaults to retry1/no SDK timeout/DirectGet=false, preserves negative retries and applies bulk replacement/unlimited timeout with last-option precedence.

A still-present logical Neutron status DOWN satisfies cloud's success policy after one accepted DELETE and one verification. Both literal DOWN and JSON-escaped equivalent are recognized; Deleted=true/Down=true while Absent=false and the actual row remains available. This is not a proof of resource disappearance or readiness.

A present Neutron row with status ACTIVE, ERROR, null, false or lowercase down does not satisfy absence/DOWN. After two default logical attempts, FloatingIPDeleteVerificationError retains requested ID, attempt count2 and the last known row; Deleted/Absent/Down remain false and no third DELETE is sent.

Actual DELETE404 returns Deleted=false without an error, verification or alternate-backend fallback in tested Neutron, Nova and source None branches for retry0/1/3/-1. The attempt remains unaccepted, NotFound exposes actual404 and Failure retains the actual failed response. Only one endpoint and one physical DELETE are used.

A first accepted DELETE204 and still-present ACTIVE verification followed by a second DELETE404 returns the source's final false result, retaining both attempts and LastVerification. The first accepted response header and second missing response body remain independently available; the second404 ends without another verification.

Nova and source None verification consume the public cloud-normalized view: a wire DOWN row with numeric ID7 is logical ACTIVE and therefore exhausts two attempts rather than satisfying DOWN. Wire retains actual DOWN. After an accepted DELETE followed by Nova list404, public lookup suppression produces absence and the delete succeeds with SuppressedNotFound retained. These tests distinguish source normalization from actual response status and do not prove IP readiness.

After a Neutron DELETE204, its independent public lookup may encounter an unfiltered Network list404 and read Nova. The tested Nova row's JSON-escaped DOWN is normalized using the configured Neutron mode and satisfies the source DOWN policy. Mutation Backend remains Neutron, verification Backend is Nova, the original list404 is retained as FallbackError, and only three logical HTTP requests occur; this is query fallback, not DELETE404 mutation fallback.

The owned delete transport preserves passive response bodies and accepts the tested source-style HTTP200/201/202/203/204/205/206/299/300/301/304/307/399 responses without a Location redirect or JSON decode requirement. With retry0 each response is one accepted mutation, retains its actual status/malformed body and returns Deleted=true without verification. These finite status fixtures do not prove every redirect/session combination or native Gophercloud default delete-code parity.

Pure concrete option preparation owns Source, nested Location pointers and project raw JSON across later caller and returned-policy mutation. A custom callback is applied once, and a later callback cannot observe an externally mutated alias from the preceding callback. The separate HTTP whole-budget fixture verifies once-applied original options across two logical attempts and nested public verification; it does not cover every callback/type/backend combination.

Pure preparation rejects nil option/context, invalid source, zero duration in the positive-timeout helper and negative bulk timeout as ErrInvalidOption. A pre-cancelled context preserves its custom cancellation cause and prevents option callbacks. Negative retry remains a supported source value rather than a negative-timeout error.

A negative retry -2 clamps to one logical DELETE with one verification; explicit additional retries3 allow four logical DELETE/verification pairs. A still-present ACTIVE row exhausts the exact max(0,retry)+1 limit with retained attempt count and Deleted=false.

Verification consumes the advertised second marker page before deciding the first accepted deletion: a late exact-ID DOWN match completes with two query pages, but late403, wrong-shaped200 collection or duplicate exact-ID matches fail without marking Verified/Deleted or issuing a second logical DELETE. Duplicate selection exposes ErrAmbiguous and actual late403 is retained in Failure.

Default UUID verification and DirectGet=true with a non-UUID ID still use public list selection; empty lists complete as absent. Explicit direct UUID verification sends a member GET: actual member404 remains an error after accepted deletion, not a mutation NotFound or successful absence. Following source getter trust, a member containing a different ID with DOWN can satisfy Down=true/Absent=false; the actual other ID stays in Wire and this result does not prove disappearance of the requested ID.

An accepted DELETE202 followed by Close failure, custom cancellation cause or cached Network API replacement retains actual accepted response/header/passive body and ResponseError202. Each mode ends after one physical DELETE with Accepted=true, Verified=false, no LastVerification and Deleted=false; Close/cancel preserve the custom cause.

After accepted DELETE204, an accepted GET200 DOWN response whose Close fails, cancels with a custom cause or changes the cached Network endpoint remains a verification error. The prior DELETE proof and LastVerification survive, GET200 ResponseError/Failure is retained, Verified/Deleted remain false and no second DELETE occurs. Close/cancel retain the custom cause.

Direct DELETE 403/503 failures retain original status/body without becoming NotFound or triggering logical retry. A native callback expanding OkCodes with404 yields one callback/two physical DELETEs but one logical attempt and a terminal SDK failure, not successful/missing deletion. A 503 callback that changes the cached Network endpoint yields one callback/one physical DELETE, retaining the original503 and blocking a second request.

Across the two-attempt DELETE/GET/DELETE/GET fixture, original delete option callbacks apply once and the result retains the entry ID despite an outside input edit. All four request deadlines are identical: default and explicit unlimited have no SDK cap, a positive timeout is nonzero, and a ten-second parent remains the exact earlier deadline. The dedicated unlimited helper clears the preceding positive timeout.

A real 60 ms SDK timeout expires while the verification request waits for its context. DeadlineExceeded is preserved after the accepted DELETE204, with exactly one DELETE and one GET, the accepted attempt still observable and Deleted=false; no further logical attempt is sent.

Connection nil/context-nil/pre-cancelled/unsafe-path-ID/nil-option preflight stops with no HTTP and no service locator, preserving a custom cancellation cause. An explicitly acquired Service whose Servers pointer is cleared in an option returns ErrInvalidOption before HTTP instead of recapturing the changed source. Legacy Nova microversion2.36 returns ErrUnsupported before mutation; its earlier explicit Compute discovery is not claimed to have locator0.

An accepted DELETE 202 whose response read returns a custom failure retains that cause, ResponseError status 202 and the partial passive body in both the accepted attempt receipt and error proof. It sends one physical DELETE, returns Deleted=false, preserves the accepted logical attempt and performs no public verification. This is bounded mutation read-error evidence, not every read/Close/backend combination.

An explicitly acquired Compute Service uses its captured Connection dependencies to select Neutron for a successful retry0 deletion. The first direct Service call locates Compute then Network and sends one DELETE; a subsequent Connection retry0 call succeeds with one more DELETE and no additional locator. This proves the tested cached dependency path without asserting shared role-cache mutation, verification or every receiver/backend policy.

differences: Go exposes a typed request and concrete options with a result separating the source boolean Deleted from actual absence, present DOWN, accepted logical attempts, last public-Get verification and failed-response evidence. An accepted DELETE is not itself verified disappearance; retry0 intentionally has no verification. This does not reproduce Python's scalar return or mutable Resource/Munch/session surface.

The delete's verification deliberately reuses ordinary cloud Get semantics rather than always using GetFloatingIPByID. Mutation backend, query fallback backend and normalization source remain distinct. Nova's source-synthetic logical ACTIVE is separated from raw Wire; a DOWN success can describe a still-existing row and never asserts an actual ACTIVE wait or deletion convergence.

Typed safe UTF-8/path IDs, explicit source/location/strict/direct-get policy and optional one shared operation timeout are Go API choices. Defaults add no SDK deadline; a bulk zero-valued options replacement sets retry0, while dedicated default preparation retains retry1. The mapping does not establish every Python dynamic retry argument, configuration or has_service/session policy.

Owned mutation transport follows the cloud-style passive HTTP200–399 response policy rather than promoting Gophercloud's native DELETE status contract. Actual response/body/header proof is retained separately from model parsing and success verification. The tested Neutron accepted Close/cancel/source and terminal retry failures preserve partial evidence, while full redirect/session/retry/default/backend combinations remain unresolved.

Direct UUID verification intentionally preserves source getter trust: a different response ID with DOWN can satisfy the source boolean, with the actual row retained and Absent=false. The result is a source success policy rather than identity-checked requested-resource disappearance. Dedicated deletion options do not add filters or expression parameters that are absent from the source deletion signature.

Selected Compute microversion2.36 or higher is rejected as ErrUnsupported before legacy Nova DELETE. The pinned cloud helper issues its legacy request and can translate an actual404 into false; Go's local version preflight is a deliberate difference and does not establish automatic endpoint/API-version negotiation or downgrade.

The declared ID/retry deletion contract is mapped. Connection/profile use_direct_get configuration is expressed as an explicit Go option with default false; typed safe IDs and int retries, exact missing-catalog fallback, guarded context/accepted-error behavior, and the local legacy version preflight are documented Go choices. Inherited mutable Resource/session/cache APIs remain separately tracked in the SDK scope rather than missing arguments of this declaration.

The fixed success policy accepts final HTTP200 through399. Unlike the source's literal status<400 comparison, final informational1xx responses are rejected; normal net/http informational handling and source session redirects are not exact Python transport parity.

contracts.behavior: Concrete preparation defaults to Wait=false, a60-second post-allocation WaitTimeout, automatic wait interval and no SDK whole-operation cap. Last-option precedence permits a zero-valued bulk replacement to clear budgets; negative wait timeout is retained for a consumed immediate timeout rather than globally rejecting ignored destination values.

Fresh Neutron creation resolves an ordinary network by member then name, without requiring router:external=true, and posts only floating_network_id plus consumed port/fixed fields. The finite lower fixtures accept200/201/202/299/399 and retain actual status/header plus an exact large-number unknown field; they do not inspect or reuse a free-IP inventory.

A nonempty explicit Neutron port bypasses even an invalid Server ref, FixedAddress and NATDestination, and invokes no named-server resolver. Its tested flat-object response is admitted. Cloud logical request seeds supply only missing network/port values while actual Wire stays unseeded, and Allocation/FloatingIP logical data do not alias.

When a Server destination is consumed, no ports or an unmatched explicit fixed literal produce an unattached allocation. A matching IPv6 literal is sent unchanged. Without an explicit fixed address, multiple ports are narrowed by NAT and the latest created_at port supplies the first parseable IPv4; malformed automatic fixed-IP items are skipped before a valid address.

Complete ports discovery precedes mutation: the tested late403, missing explicit NAT and no usable IPv4 paths send no allocation POST. Default external selection uses the shared role candidate or, when unavailable, the first enabled router gateway, skipping a disabled router.

Without Server or explicit port, FixedAddress/NATDestination and Wait=true with a negative wait timeout are ignored. This accepted unattached allocation sends no poll or cleanup; a missing response ID is logical null while Wire preserves actual absence.

For configured Nova and None, nil Network reads the first pool, while explicit empty or named Network is a literal pool with no pool query. Creation is fresh POST followed by the mandatory raw member compatibility GET of numeric ID7; ignored Server/fixed/NAT/wait values do not trigger attachment or readiness work. The tested response permits null address and a different pool/attached instance rather than imposing assignment-candidate validation.

The final Nova compatibility response is normalized through the shared cloud normalizer, not the fresh allocation candidate verifier. The new HTTP tests keep wire ERROR and exact vendor numbers beside source-synthetic logical ACTIVE. Existing shared pure normalization assertions cover canonical/null alias precedence, strict/non-strict aliases, properties/location ownership and configured-Neutron mode after Nova fallback; this is composition evidence, not additional new Create fixtures.

Pure Neutron NotFound before accepted allocation can fall through from missing ordinary-network lookup or allocation POST to Nova. The original error and configured-Neutron normalization remain visible. A nonempty explicit port instead returns ErrUnsupported before any Nova allocation, and the tested fallback discovery is Network then Compute.

An accepted Neutron POST202 with malformed JSON, Close error, custom caller cancellation or cached Network endpoint drift retains Allocated=true and actual allocation status/header/envelope with ResponseError202. It sends no wait, cleanup, compatibility GET or alternate allocation; tested Close/cancel/source causes remain observable.

Nova compatibility403 or an accepted malformed compatibility model preserves the initial accepted allocation and the actual compatibility failure. Accepted Nova POST with null or object-valued ID retains raw Allocation and ResponseError200 but performs no unsafe compatibility request, cleanup or concealed reallocation.

Present null, false or different response port overrides the request seed. No-wait creation returns an error beside its actual accepted201 receipt and unchanged response port in Wire/logical Resource; no cleanup occurs.

With a selected port and Wait=true, the ordinary public-Get loop polls immediately, continues past an empty list and logical ERROR, accepts JSON-semantic exact ACTIVE, then verifies the selected port. The successful fixture retains three observations; lookup403 or final port mismatch returns a known allocation without cleanup, Waited success or Nova compatibility.

Direct UUID wait uses the public member GET. A member404 after an accepted Neutron allocation retains that allocation and observation, with no Nova fallback, second allocation or timeout cleanup. This is the deliberate post-acceptance safety boundary.

A consumed zero/negative or real20-ms SDK wait timeout returns FloatingIPCreateTimeoutError with the allocated ID and DeadlineExceeded. Cleanup runs one default-policy DELETE and public absence verification on the still-live original context rather than the expired wait child. Successful absence and cleanup403 are separate results; original lookup/POST and cleanup DELETE have no SDK wait-child deadline.

Caller custom cancellation during a public wait remains Canceled with its cause and accepted allocation, without detached cleanup. Expiry of a20-ms overall cap is DeadlineExceeded but not FloatingIPCreateTimeoutError and sends no cleanup; the SDK distinguishes this earlier budget from its own post-allocation wait timer.

Bulk factories own Source/Location pointers and project raw JSON; returned policy edits do not mutate retained factory data. Original option callbacks run once. Preparation rejects nil options, invalid source, nonpositive dedicated overall timeout/interval and negative bulk interval; a pre-cancelled context preserves its cause and invokes no callback.

A direct Compute Service captures its source before original callbacks and snapshots request Network before a callback changes the caller string. The tested earlier parent deadline remains exact on lookup/allocation, and a subsequent Connection call reuses already selected Compute/Network dependencies without another locator. Clearing the captured Servers collection in an original option fails before HTTP.

The initial cloud allocation success policy cannot be expanded by a native retry callback: expanded404 remains a terminal failure after two physical POST attempts, without allocation acceptance or Nova fallback. Changing the cached endpoint in that callback stops before the second physical POST and retains ErrInvalidOption; original callbacks are invoked once.

differences: Only the named cloud create_floating_ip declaration is mapped: fresh Neutron/Nova allocation, consumed Neutron destination/wait/port checks, Nova compatibility fetch and SDK-wait-timeout cleanup. Independent availability, DeleteUnattached, attach/detach, native/Proxy operations and inherited Resource/session/cache APIs retain their own tracking and are not requirements missing from this signature.

Go replaces arbitrary supplied Python Server/Resource/Munch objects with safe resource.Ref ID/name selectors and concrete option factories. Typed string fixed/NAT/port inputs, owned JSON views/actual Wire and structured allocation/compatibility/observation/cleanup evidence are deliberate API mappings rather than Python object identity or exception/return-value equivalence.

Network pointer presence preserves Nova None versus empty pool while Neutron nil/empty both select defaults. Source None explicitly creates through Nova. Typed invalid path IDs and unknown source/interval/budget policies return local errors; ignored destination values are validated only on their consuming branch. Dynamic Python numeric/object inputs, unsafe/null routing and timeout=None TypeError corner are not exposed.

Neutron Resource.create request seeds are projected only into missing returned keys and never actual Wire. Flat object and named object responses are supported; malformed JSON, wrong-shaped envelopes and unusable executable IDs retain accepted proof and fail rather than reproducing Python Resource malformed-body swallowing or unsafe URL stringification. Present response null remains authoritative.

Python catches Neutron helper NotFound even after accepted allocation and may allocate again through Nova. Go permits only pure pre-acceptance absence fallback and rejects mixed/terminal source/context/processing/native retry failures; post-acceptance errors cannot hide a second allocation. This intentional mutation-safety mapping is documented and regression tested.

Go uses a library-owned child context for the post-allocation60-second wait, with optional positive interval and separate whole-operation cap. It interrupts in-flight HTTP and performs a final guard rather than copying Python wall-clock yield/sleep late-success behavior. Only its own wait-timeout cause with a live original guarded context triggers cleanup; parent/whole timeout or caller cancellation never detaches deletion.

Timeout cleanup reuses the mapped public Delete default retry1 and ordinary Get semantics. Python logs cleanup exceptions and rethrows only ResourceTimeout; Go retains Cleanup/CleanupError and joins the original typed timeout, transport and context causes. DOWN policy success is not actual absence, and no unrelated cleanup operation is implied.

Legacy Nova is checked against the selected Compute microversion below2.36 without a hidden downgrade. Its final view uses the configured cloud normalization mode: direct Nova/None may synthesize logical ACTIVE while actual Wire remains unchanged, and configured-Neutron fallback remains Neutron mode. This function does not promise real Nova lifecycle/readiness or full endpoint/version negotiation.

Automatic destination selection keeps source-style created_at lexical reverse order and the first valid IPv4 while explicit fixed selection is literal and can be IPv6. Typed parsing and stable string order replace arbitrary Python malformed or mixed created_at/object comparison corners. Ordinary canonical HTTP/model behavior is mapped without reproducing every dynamic Resource descriptor/runtime case.

Owned allocation/compatibility transport accepts final HTTP200 through399, preserving actual status/body/header and guarded native retries. Source literal status<400 also includes informational1xx; normal net/http informational handling and redirect/session combinations are deliberate transport boundaries, not claims of exact Python session behavior. Standard query/lookup reads retain their documented typed status/envelope/paging rules.

Go exposes explicit per-call source/location/strict/direct-get options and existing immutable Connection configuration. Generic Python has_service negotiation, arbitrary mutable session/profile overrides and inherited Resource/cache/discovery facilities remain separate SDK goal scope, rather than an unimplemented declared Create argument.

contracts.behavior: The Neutron cleanup finishes a two-page unfiltered public inventory before any DELETE, preserves source order, skips an attached row with an unusable ID and sends no If-Match revision header. Its exact sequence is two inventory GETs, DELETE a/public-Get absence verification, then DELETE b/public-Get verification; only Network is located. Count2/AllDeleted=true and the owned two-page inventory, accepted204/verified attempts and absence flags are retained.

Configured Nova/None returns a successful ineligible zero without any locator or HTTP. Clean Network endpoint absence locates only Network and skips inventory/Compute/delete. A mixed absence plus terminal catalog cause remains an error with that cause and no aggregate success. Empty or attached-only eligible inventory returns Count0/AllDeleted=true after one Network list and no DELETE; the whitespace port remains attached.

A first clean DELETE404 records an unaccepted false and still processes later candidates; a second logical DELETE404 after accepted deletion/ACTIVE verification similarly preserves both attempts and continues. Both completed false-containing runs keep all three items, Count2 and AllDeleted=false with no error. Actual DELETE403 or verification403 stops at the second item, retains Count1 and the failed item proof, and never deletes the third candidate.

The original options execute once across two candidate items and observe default retry1. Retry1 adds one logical DELETE for the first still-ACTIVE IP, retry3 adds three, retry0 makes one passive accepted DELETE per item with no verification, and negative retry-2 makes one DELETE with verification. Nonzero verification finishes on logical DOWN and the exact request/attempt totals are asserted; Count2/AllDeleted=true reflects the mapped per-item boolean rather than actual disappearance.

Candidate selection consumes public Resource port_id with JSON truthiness. Tested missing/null/empty-string/false/zero/empty-array/empty-object produce seven ordered deletions, while whitespace/string-zero/nonzero-number/nonempty-array/nonempty-object rows with unsafe IDs are skipped. Missing Neutron port is logical null and remains absent from actual Wire, including Strict=true.

A clean Neutron inventory404 can fall back to numeric-ID7 Nova inventory normalized under configured Neutron. Nonstrict view supplies the null port_id alias and the subsequent DELETE still targets captured Neutron /floatingips/7, not the inventory Nova backend. Strict fallback instead lacks port_id and returns ErrInvalidOption before DELETE, preserving Eligible, inventory/fallback proof, Count0 and AllDeleted=false.

Incomplete public inventory never deletes an eligible prefix: tested early403, first-row descriptor failure, later403, wrong-shaped later200, continuation cycle, accepted later Close error, cached endpoint drift and caller cancellation all leave Items empty, Count0, AllDeleted=false and no DELETE. Consumed page proof remains; physical403 or accepted200 ResponseError/Failure and custom Close/cancellation/source causes are distinguished.

Executable IDs are consumed sequentially only after port eligibility. A later unsafe or missing ID errors before that DELETE while preserving the earlier completed/accepted item and Count1, plus the bad selected Resource with Deletion=nil and Item.Error. Duplicate a,a,c remains three ordered calls: the second a404 is a false item and processing continues to c, returning Count2/AllDeleted=false. Attached unsafe IDs are never consumed for deletion.

After candidate a completes, candidate b accepted202 with Close failure, cached Network API replacement, custom caller cancellation or a real25-ms operation expiry retains its passive body/accepted response and202 ResponseError but is not counted as deleted. Count1 and the two items remain, no candidate c is deleted, and Close/cancel/source/DeadlineExceeded causes remain observable. No verification is performed under the prepared retry0 policy.

One absolute deadline spans the inventory and all candidate deletions rather than resetting per item. The fixtures assert no deadline for default/unlimited, a nonzero shared deadline for explicit timeout, exact earlier one-minute parent deadline under a two-minute SDK cap, and unlimited clearing a previous cap. Successful retry0 runs complete three items; the real25-ms boundary preserves partial progress instead of detaching later work.

Bulk Source/Location factories retain the original Neutron/source project facts despite later caller pointer/raw-byte mutation. Callback count is one per aggregate call. Each selected duplicate row independently owns Resource/Wire; mutating one item or its verification model leaves inventory, the other item, its Wire and independent response headers unchanged. Reusing the same factory after output mutation restores original scope/name and succeeds again.

Nil Connection/Service and nil context/option, invalid source, dedicated zero timeout, negative bulk timeout or pre-cancelled context fail before HTTP/locator and preserve typed/cancellation causes, even for a source-None skip. A directly acquired Service whose original option clears the captured Servers pointer fails before HTTP rather than recapturing the replacement; its earlier explicit Compute discovery is recorded rather than claimed to have locator0.

A completed lower Delete=true stays in aggregate Count even when an injected later aggregate operation guard fails. The finite final-guard injection scan requires reaching at least one completed item, keeps Count1 and AllDeleted=false, preserves the guard cause, and never sends more than one DELETE. Accepted-but-failed lower deletion remains a separate uncounted case.

A successfully acquired Compute Service and a later Connection cleanup reuse the same cached Connection dependencies. Both calls override configured source None with per-call Neutron, complete two default-retry items with public absence verification, execute original options once per call and retain exact Compute-then-Network locator count without rediscovery. Each five-request inventory/delete/verification sequence shares a nonzero minute cap; item errors remain nil and actual Neutron verification pages are retained.

differences: The named cleanup declaration has only retry=1. Go reuses concrete Delete options and returns an owned result separating eligibility, complete inventory proof, ordered item decisions/deletion results, a count of completed Deleted=true items, aggregate AllDeleted and an optional item Error. Python returns int Count if all candidate booleans succeed, False after any clean false, or raises and discards earlier booleans on an exception.

Empty or ineligible cleanup maps the actual source all([]) integer0 to Count=0/AllDeleted=true, despite the source docstring saying False if none. Go additionally retains a partial successful Count on a false or error, including a lower Delete already completed before a later aggregate guard error; accepted lower requests whose processing/verification failed are not counted.

Eligibility uses configured Neutron and a captured lazy Network binding. Pure endpoint absence is an empty skip; mixed source/context/catalog failures propagate instead of reproducing broad Python has_service exception swallowing. Explicit Nova/None never makes this function clean up Nova floating IPs. Generic has_service/session/config negotiation remains separately tracked.

Candidates consume the public Resource port_id with ordinary JSON truthiness, rather than Wire-only fields or canonical port/attached aliases. Strict Nova fallback lacks the compatibility port_id and raises a typed structural error, preserving the source attribute-access failure. Configured Neutron remains the DELETE backend even if the public inventory falls back to Nova.

IDs are consumed sequentially only for unattached rows from public Resource data. Owned passive nullable/malformed IDs remain in Inventory/item proof, while unsafe/null/container executable identities return local typed errors before that DELETE. Arbitrary Python object coercions and Resource-like executable dictionaries are not exposed.

All caller options are prepared once and one optional whole-operation deadline covers backend selection, complete inventory, every per-IP retry and verification. Source/context guards and independently cloned selected rows/actual HTTP proof are explicit Go semantics; no caller cancellation is bypassed for detached cleanup.

Per-IP deletion retains the mapped standalone Delete contract: exact retry0 skips verification, negative retry performs one DELETE plus verification, default1 adds one logical attempt, no sleep, DELETE404 false continues the aggregate loop, and public Get absence/DOWN succeeds. DOWN or retry0 true is a source boolean policy rather than identity-checked physical disappearance.

The named workflow is a snapshot inventory followed by ordered deletions, not an atomic association revalidation or revision-aware purge. The pinned two-step create/attach race note still applies. Independent Create/availability/attach/detach/native/Proxy/mutable Resource/session APIs are separate SDK scope and are not missing declared arguments of this cleanup.

Existing typed query envelope/status/continuation and legacy Compute microversion checks remain documented Go policies. Selected Nova microversion>=2.36 is unsupported without hidden downgrade if a fallback query is actually required; final informational1xx/session redirect combinations and malformed Python runtime corners are not exact transport parity.

contracts.behavior: Pinned _proxy.py:114-127 dispatches one Container metadata fetch. The concrete Fetch lane executes one fixed explicit-ID GET containers/{RequestID} with no body/query/list/name lookup under the fixture's provider policy. Foreign response refs are passive, and changing or nil-ing public Resources does not redirect or redefine this owned request; Name is rejected before HTTP.

The declared Container view preserves untyped name/status/type and raw created/updated values. secret_refs and consumers preserve arbitrary JSON elements, wrap non-null scalar/object values in a singleton list, and distinguish missing/null from empty arrays. Known client aliases are accepted only when the canonical key is absent; canonical null wins. Wire remains the original object with unknown/self/case-variant values and exact large integers.

RequestID and Ref() keep the original executable ID separately from Resource.Body.id and nullable ContainerID. A missing response id preserves the request seed and a present id/null replaces it without rerouting. The shared passive HREF formatter takes the last raw path component, preserves percent spelling and a trailing empty component, excludes query/fragment, and returns null for missing/null; invalid or nonstring refs retain the actual response proof.

Leaf and cached Connection fixtures share the authenticated provider and selected reverse ResourceBase. Tokens rotated after API creation, source headers, operation headers and selected microversion remain effective. Resource/Wire/Envelope/Header are owned snapshots. Option slices and intermediate header maps are cloned and callbacks run once; captured route/provider/version or cancellation changes stop before later options/HTTP, and a native retry route change stops before a second request while retaining the original503 cause.

Actual403/404 remain native HTTP errors with original body/header and Fetch operation/resource cause under the default fixture policy. Successful203/302 preserve actual status; accepted malformed/empty/non-object/non-UTF8 bodies and HREF formatter errors retain actual response evidence. The shared engine's complete known-object read/Close failure and post-response source/custom-cancellation failure return receipt and possible Wire with Resource=nil, preserve original/custom causes, close the tracked body once, invoke no native retry and perform no SDK composition resend. Pre-cancel and nil/invalid source/ref/options fail before HTTP.

differences: Concrete resource.Ref and the fetched value's Ref() replace Python's ID-string or mutable Resource input. Only an explicit, valid single URL-path segment is executable; Name and full-HREF refs fail before HTTP. RequestID remains the route even when response id or passive refs differ. Arbitrary Resource/subclass/seeded-instance overloads remain separate lifecycle scope rather than a missing declared getter input.

The owned Resource view projects declared Body attributes and coercions while Wire and Envelope preserve the actual object, including unknown/self/case-variant fields, null/presence and exact large JSON numbers. This independently owned result replaces the mutable Python Resource and its dynamic descriptor/cache/instance state; generated native Get retains its previous alias and return type.

Canonical wire keys, including present null, deterministically precede client attribute aliases in Go. Pinned Resource._consume_attrs follows input insertion order for conflicting aliases. The reused Go HREF parser is stricter than urllib.urlsplit for some authorities; the formatter still treats refs as passive strings and preserves percent spelling and trailing empty path components.

Resource.Body.location is null. Pinned Proxy._get_resource at proxy.py:583-596 passes connection=conn to a new ID Resource, and Resource initialization at resource.py:838-839 may seed computed location from conn.current_location even without project_id/availability_zone. This concrete authenticated-ServiceClient getter does not synthesize that Connection location.

Go accepts final HTTP200..399 object responses and preserves actual status, including the tested203 and302 without Location. Pinned exceptions.raise_from_response allows statuses below400 and generic Resource._translate_response can suppress JSON ValueError. Go deliberately returns an accepted ResponseError plus receipt for empty/malformed/non-object/non-UTF8 responses or formatter failures instead of returning a seed-only Resource.

Context and WithFetchHeader are concrete Go inputs; no SDK timeout is added, and body/query/argument extensions are unsupported. Captured source guards and fixed requests retain the configured shared provider/live token and native retry/reauthentication policy. SDK composition errors do not introduce name fallback, deletion or resend. Generic session/cache negotiation and inherited lifecycle are tracked separately.

Completion is restricted to python:key_manager/v1/get_container. Native Container Get/List/CRUD, Proxy list/Find/wait and Resource lifecycle/session declarations are not promoted by this named getter mapping. The six offline Go HTTP groups use existing common fixtures/testhelper/body fault adapters; they are not authenticated OpenStack or Python execution evidence.

contracts.behavior: Pinned _proxy.py:220-231 dispatches one Order metadata fetch. Foreign response refs are passive, and changing or nil-ing public Resources does not redirect or redefine this owned request; Name is rejected before HTTP.

The declared Order view preserves inherited name, untyped creator/status/substatus/type and raw created/updated values. meta retains arbitrary nested dictionaries and exact large integers; non-null non-dict values become {}, while missing/null remain null.
